correctness.rationale: PASS: The matrix-tree minor equals det[L(C_n)+tI]=2[T_n(1+t/2)−1]; logarithmic derivatives give the exact Bernoulli spectral variance. The hyperbolic form proves Vʹ_n(2)>0 and V_n/n→v(t)=2√t/(t+4)^(3/2) in C² on compacts. Quantitative small/large t tail bounds force all global maximizers near the unique limiting peak t=2. Strict concavity there yields eventual global uniqueness; Vʹ_n(2)~n³ρ^n/(3√3) and vʺ(2)=−1/(36√3) yield factor 12 and the sharp peak deficit. Independently verified determinant/Chebyshev and variance identities for n=3,4,5,6,8,10; 90-digit optimization checked asymptotic approach at n=10,15,20,25,30. Finite optimization alone is not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: PASS: Optimizing hub-degree uncertainty under a single natural conductance control is a motivated stochastic-network design problem. Eventual uniqueness and a sharp exponentially small finite-wheel bias quantify a genuine boundary invisible in the prior general variance formula; no invented explicit finite-n cutoff.

final_claim: For weighted wheel W_(n+1) with rim edges conductance one and common spoke conductance t>0, the spoke-count variance has, for all sufficiently large n, exactly one global maximizing t_n>2; (t_n−2)/(n²(2−√3)^n)→12 and max variance equals n/(3√3)−(2/3)n²(2−√3)^n(1+o(1)). Its exact spectral variance is a known preliminary formula, not claimed as novel.
limitations: Existing determinant/spectral degree-variance identity is previously covered; no novelty attributed to it.
Double-precision optimizers fail to resolve displacements below ~10⁻⁸; high-precision checks used for finite illustration and asymptotic limit is proved analytically.
